analysis.title: Market volatility reinforces the case for portfolio resilience
key_insights: US equities fell again on Thursday (Nov 19) as AI-trade concerns combined with a more hawkish rate backdrop. The S&P 500 closed down 2% and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3%. All major S&P 500 sectors fell and decliners substantially outnumbered advancers on the NYSE and Nasdaq.
Recent selling followed persistent pressure on chipmakers and cloud companies as investors question the scale of investment needed to build AI infrastructure.

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting indicated nearly all policymakers expected further tightening to be necessary if the economy evolves as anticipated. Markets priced a near certainty of a 25bp hike in December.
Gold fell to a 14-month low around USD 3,654 an ounce on higher rate expectations and dollar strength. US 2-year and 10-year yields fell 4bps and 2bps respectively while the dollar rose modestly.

Hunterbrook published a short-sell report on AMD (-7.7%) over fears its China business may be affected by stricter US chip restrictions. NVIDIA fell 3.3% despite an upbeat revenue forecast earlier in the week.

UBS base case for 2027 is growth close to trend, rising corporate profits, more AI investment and moderating inflation later in the year. It says the economic expansion, earnings cycle and structural AI investment story have not broken.

UBS recently downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral, citing elevated expectations, high index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes. The AI debate is shifting from whether investment continues to whether it can generate enough revenue and shareholder returns.

UBS estimates cumulative US technology AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by end-2028, and that AI model and application revenues must reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return. Competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models may threaten returns.
UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December and March but not a prolonged tightening cycle. Cumulative higher rates should weigh on consumer demand and base effects should moderate underlying inflation.

Equity positioning: UBS expects around 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027, but the top 10 companies are 39% of the index, so small changes in expectations for a few AI-linked businesses can have an outsized effect. Eurozone is the preferred region (15% 2027 earnings growth forecast, lower valuation than the US). Sector preferences are industrials and health care, and US equal-weight strategies can reduce tech concentration.

Within US tech, UBS favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible AI monetization plus select leaders in compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software. It is cautious on leveraged capacity providers, lower-quality suppliers and companies whose valuations depend on persistent bottlenecks or distant cash flows.

Fixed income: UBS favors intermediate duration (2 to 10 years) and quality bonds, with the best return opportunity in EM and high yield. EM sovereign and corporate bonds yield about 7.1% and 7.0%, and US high yield about 8.3%.

UBS recommends using volatility: structured strategies can limit losses, generate income or allow measured participation, and higher implied volatility may raise their appeal, with diversification and careful sizing advised.
